title: Price offsets by vendor risk profile — questionnaire-autocomplete & contract template experiment
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Summary: Run a bounded experiment that ties a lightweight vendor security questionnaire autopopulation flow to a simple pricing offset calculator and a set of templated contract addenda. Goal is to reduce friction for low-risk SMB suppliers and surface transparent insurance/coverage recommendations for higher-risk vendors so procurement cycles shorten and legal effort is concentrated where it matters.

Background: Current onboarding is heavy: full SOC2 evidence collection and manual legal redlines for many small vendors. This raises procurement lead time and negotiation overhead. Several previous initiatives explored minimal SOC2-lite packages and evidence collectors, but we lack a connected experiment that (a) reduces friction for low-risk vendors via an autocomplete Q&A, (b) computes an immediate provisional pricing offset (credit) tied to documented risk controls, and (c) pushes a pre-approved contract addendum to streamline legal acceptance.

Objectives:
- Reduce time-to-contract for SMB vendors by 30% in experiment cohort.
- Increase proportion of self-serve approvals (no manual legal review) for vendors assessed as 'low risk' by at least 20 percentage points.
- Surface clear insurance recommendations for medium/high risk vendors and measure uptake.

Hypotheses:
H1: A guided questionnaire that pre-fills common answers from supplied artifacts (SSO attestations, GitHub, package manifests) will reduce task completion time by 40% and reduce abandoned onboarding flows.
H2: Showing a transparent price-offset (insurance credit or discount) tied to risk profile increases vendor willingness to accept standard contract templates and reduces negotiation requests.
H3: A small set of pre-approved addenda covering data handling and liability will shift ~50% of 'low risk' vendors to self-approval.

Experiment design / Approach:
1) Selection: Identify 120 SMB vendors in the intake queue over 6 weeks, split 60 control / 60 experiment. Control = current intake workflow. Experiment = new flow.
2) Questionnaire Autocomplete: Implement server-side heuristics to pre-fill answers when vendors connect a repo, provide audit artifacts, or complete a quick attestation. Keep manual override.
3) Risk Scoring -> Offset Calculator: Produce a simple risk score (low/medium/high) from questionnaire + artifacts. Map to a deterministic price offset table (e.g., low=5% credit, medium=0%, high=no credit + insurance recommendation). Display the calculated offset before contract acceptance.
4) Contract Addenda Pack: Legal provides 3 lightweight, pre-approved addenda (data-processing, incident SLA, limited liability) that can be appended by self-serve for low-risk vendors; medium/high require legal review queue.
5) Metrics & Telemetry: Track time-to-complete, drop-off, % self-approve, # legal touchpoints, negotiation messages, and insurance recommendation uptake.

Success metrics:
- Primary: Median time-to-contract (experiment vs control) and % self-serve approvals for low-risk vendors.
- Secondary: Drop-off rate during intake; # of legal escalations avoided; vendor NPS (post-onboarding 1-2 weeks).

Scope / Out of scope:
- In scope: Questionnaire UI changes, autocomplete heuristics, simple deterministic risk->offset mapping, three addenda templates, instrumentation and dashboards for the experiment cohort.
- Out of scope: Full SOC2 audit automation, custom contract negotiations for enterprise vendors, changes to pricing tiers for existing customers (this is vendor onboarding pricing offsets only).

Deliverables:
- Product: new intake flow with autocomplete, offset display, addenda acceptance flow.
- Legal: three pre-approved addenda in DocuSign-ready format.
- Eng: heuristic service + risk scoring endpoint, instrumentation, and rollout guardrails.
- Metrics: dashboard in Redash showing experiment KPIs.
- Docs: playbook for solutions and sales to explain offset logic and legal boundaries.

Timeline (high-level):
- Week 1 (Feb 17-23): Spec, legal templates, engineering spike.
- Week 2 (Feb 24-Mar 2): Implement autocomplete backend + risk scoring.
- Week 3 (Mar 3-9): UX, addenda integration, instrumentation.
- Week 4-6 (Mar 10-31): Run experiment, monitor, interim check-ins.
- Week 7 (Apr 1-4): Analyze results, retro, recommendation.

Risks and mitigations:
- False confidence from autopopulated answers may cause misclassification: require explicit vendor attestation and audit sampling (random 5% of low-risk cases).
- Legal boundary creep: keep addenda intentionally narrow and time-limited; legal holds final sign-off prior to rollout.
- Customer confusion about pricing offsets: surface clear, line-item explanation and link to support/contract FAQ.

Stakeholders:
- PM: Sofia Martinez (owner)
- Eng lead: Liam Chen (assignee)
- Legal: Priya Nair (template owner)
- Security review: Ethan Reynolds (security reviewer)
- Solutions / Sales: Kara Blake (field comms)

Acceptance criteria:
- Experiment flow implemented behind a feature flag and available to the selected cohort.
- Dashboards instrumented and capturing required metrics.
- Legal addenda uploaded and capable of being appended in the acceptance flow.
- Security sign-off for data collection and storage of vendor artifacts.

Notes:
- This is intended as a shipping experiment to evaluate a pricing/packaging lever tied to procurement risk, not a permanent pricing change. If successful we will propose a scalable policy and contract policy matrix for enterprise adoption.
